title.narrative: UNHABITAT innovative solutions for IDPS II
UNHABITAT innovative solutions for IDPS II

description.narrative:
Somalia is one of the fastest urbanizing countries in the world. The rapid urbanization is caused by significant forced displacements from rural areas into urban areas driven by conflicts, insecurity, search for economic opportunities and cyclical environmental adversities such as drought and famine. This has a huge impact not only upon livelihood opportunities, peace and stability and resilience, but also shifting rural and pastoralist livelihood to urban economies. The urban influx raises many challenges for the provision of basic urban services including secure access to land for settlement of IDPs and existing vulnerable communities. Lack of effective land administration and planning systems and weak institutions has led to arbitrary distribution of land and has aggravated contestation over land, housing and basic services. Intense competition over land exacerbates forced evictions particularly among IDPs and urban poor.
The focus of this programme will be to promote inclusive employment opportunities for urban vulnerable populations, increase youth participation; integration of displacement affected households and to strengthen implementation of Durable Solutions and Youth development across Somalia. The programme will be implemented in Mogadishu, Kismayo, Baidoa and Dollow which are some of the majorly affected towns/cities.

Somalia är ett av de länder i världen där urbaniseringen går snabbast. Orsaken till att många flyttar från rurala till urbana områden är att det råder konflikter, instabilitet, brist på försörjningsmöjligheter samt återkommande miljörelaterade händelser som torka och svält. Detta har stor påverkan, inte bara på människors försörjningsmöjligheter, fred, stabilitet och resiliens, det är också en utmaning för människor att övergå från en jordbruks- till en urban ekonomi. Inflyttningen till städerna skapar utmaningar för tillhandahållandet av basala urbana tjänster, bland annat tillgången till mark för internflyktingar och andra sårbara grupper. Bristen på fungerande markadministration och planeringssystem samt svaga institutioner har lett till en godtycklig fördelning av mark, vilket spätt på dispyter om mark, bostäder och basala samhällstjänster. Stor konkurrens om mark leder till fler tvångsavhysningar, som speciellt drabbar internflyktingar och fattiga i städer.
Fokus för detta program kommer att vara att främja inkluderande sysselsättningsmöjligheter för sårbara befolkningsgrupper i städer, öka delaktigheten bland ungdomar; integrera flyktingfamiljer samt stärka införandet av hållbara lösningar och främja ungdomars utveckling i Somalia. Programmet ska genomföras i Mogadishu, Kismayo, Baidoa och Dollow, som är några av de mest påverkade städerna.

The main objective of the project is to:
To contribute to sustainable urban development, building resilient communities and providing urban services and livelihood opportunities for residents and marginalised groups.
The project has 4 main outcomes: Outcome 1: Inclusive employment opportunities in market sector driven value chains under the sustainable productive sectors increased. Outcome 2: Increased youth participation in peacebuilding and reconciliation efforts including engagement in local governance and national decision-making processes. Outcome 3: Enhanced local social, economic and spatial integration of displacement affected households through urban regeneration and upgrading projects. Outcome 4: Enhancing tools and frameworks that strengthen implementation of Durable Solutions and Youth development across Somalia.

The project has made some progress as follows:
In relation to outcome 1, the programme effectively increased employment opportunities in market-driven value chains within sustainable productive sectors. The construction training manual was upgraded, and both a sustainability strategy for the youth center and a youth engagement strategy were developed, ensuring long-term impact. As a result, 550 youth received training and certification, enhancing their employability, with many securing entry to the job market.
In outcome 2, the programme improved youth participation in peacebuilding and reconciliation efforts, as well as engagement in local governance and national decision-making processes. Essential spaces for youth were created, and capacity assessments of youth-led organizations were conducted. Workshops were organized, and a youth network was selected to support the Baidoa Youth Centre. Capacity building efforts reached 50 youth, enhancing their skills and involvement. The Baidoa Youth Centre engaged in income-generating activities to sustain the facility. This includes hiring out the renovated football pitch, leasing training rooms to humanitarian organizations and ministries, and leasing the cafeteria. Additionally, the computer lab charges a registration fee while offering free classes, and youth organizations hold engagement sessions at no additional cost. A website was created for Baidoa Youth Centre that is functioning and updated.
With regards to outcome 3 and 4, the programme achieved several accomplishments. With the construction housing resource pooling and shared labor minimized delays and empowered beneficiaries, allowing for more efficient project completion. A community-driven approach facilitated active participation in construction of housing. Beneficiaries were empowered to negotiate material costs, and the establishment of storage facilities safeguarded materials from adverse weather conditions. Additionally, securing land for shelter construction and implementing drainage systems on challenging terrain contributed significantly to the project's sustainability. House, Land and Property training was provided to beneficiaries enhanced their skills and knowledge, improving their ability to address housing, land, and property issues effectively and contributing to more equitable and sustainable community development.
In short, the programme impacted a total of 20 395 people.
